inputs: All synthetic fixtures; source:live exercises only validation code paths.

results.name: Unconfigured and explicitly disabled modes always retain baseline
Malformed configuration containers and unsupported modes fail closed
Missing or true kill switch overrides allowlist and 100 percent
Only an explicit lowercase false opens the kill-switch gate
Malformed actors cannot enter even an all-user cohort
Rollout and revision identifiers are required and bounded
Percent requires an integer string from zero through one hundred
Zero and one hundred percent honor both endpoints for every sampled actor
Allowlist selects only listed owners at zero percent and normalizes case
Malformed, duplicate and excessive allowlists never partially admit an actor
Cohorts are deterministic across requests, revision changes and UUID case
Increasing percentage preserves all previously selected actors
A deliberate new rollout identifier produces a distinct stable cohort
Selection uses its supplied server config and never mutates it or exposes actor IDs
Complete healthy fixture yields review eligibility, never approval
Synthetic evidence remains hold even with critical counters
Evidence must match the exact candidateSha
Evidence must match the exact deploymentId
Evidence must match the exact rolloutId
Evidence must match the exact configRevision
Malformed expected identities fail closed without reflecting their input
Unknown evidence properties and arbitrary source claims are rejected
Clock and observation boundaries are checked before interpreting incidents
Short, stale and undersampled windows stay on hold
Observation duration and freshness accept their exact documented boundaries
UTC offsets describe the same window without changing its result
Counters cannot exceed requests or contain fractional and nonfinite data
Nonempty cohorts require observed actors and latency
Empty cohorts are valid insufficient samples, never invented latency or model usage
Observed maximum is mandatory and cannot contradict the call total
Successful answers with zero provider calls cannot earn eligibility
Baseline has no fallback path and swarm success requires all three agents
Failed requests may legitimately stop before making any provider call
Started fallbacks count their attempted baseline calls even when all fail
Failure, regression, fallback and latency thresholds are inclusive at the boundary
Absolute failure rate independently requests rollback
A small absolute failure rate still rolls back when regression exceeds the limit
Fallback rate belongs to the assigned swarm cohort
Both absolute and comparative p95 latency limits enforce rollback
One authBoundary incident requires rollback without a minimum sample
One crossUserContext incident requires rollback without a minimum sample
One unconfirmedWrite incident requires rollback without a minimum sample
One canonicalAction incident requires rollback without a minimum sample
One dataLoss incident requires rollback without a minimum sample
One callBudget incident requires rollback without a minimum sample
A valid but old critical incident remains a conservative rollback recommendation
Per-request baseline excess cannot hide behind an acceptable average
Swarm maximum catches a fifth call even when aggregate usage stays low
A fourth call without any fallback cannot pass the aggregate gate
Each additional aggregate call needs an actual started fallback
Evidence and expected identity remain unchanged and raw metrics are not reflected
CLI returns read-only eligibility with exit zero and preserves input files
CLI uses exit one for rollback and exit two for synthetic hold
CLI help describes recommendations rather than applying changes
CLI rejects missing, duplicate and unexpected arguments without echoing them
CLI safely rejects invalid JSON, oversized files, missing files and non-files
